# awesome-ai-contribution-policies

A machine-readable dataset of how 101 open source projects treat AI-assisted and agent-written contributions.

[![CI](https://github.com/ahmad-punch/awesome-ai-contribution-policies/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ahmad-punch/awesome-ai-contribution-policies/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Code: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/code-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Data: CC BY 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/data-CC%20BY%204.0-lightgrey.svg)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
![Node >= 20](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20-339933.svg)

```console
$ jq -r '.[] | select(.repo == "kubernetes/kubernetes") | .stance, .disclosure_format, .co_author_trailer_for_ai' policies.json
disclose-required
One sentence in the PR description
forbidden
```

## Why

Projects disagree sharply about AI-written code. Some ban it, some want an `Assisted-by:` trailer, and some forbid exactly that trailer and want one sentence in the PR body instead. Getting it wrong gets a PR closed or an account blocked. The rules live in CONTRIBUTING files, AGENTS.md files, PR templates, mailing-list votes and blog posts. This repo collects them in one validated JSON file so people and tools can check before they open a PR.

Every entry was last verified on or before 2026-10-21. Policies change fast; always read the linked source before contributing.

## Summary

| Stance | Projects | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| [Ban](#ban) | 9 | AI-generated contributions are refused, sometimes with narrow exceptions. |
| [Restricted](#restricted) | 2 | AI may assist, but creating code or running agents is limited or forbidden. |
| [Disclosure required](#disclosure-required) | 20 | AI help is allowed if you declare it in the format the project asks for. |
| [Disclosure encouraged](#disclosure-encouraged) | 3 | AI help is allowed; declaring it is appreciated but optional. |
| [Neutral](#neutral) | 17 | The project addresses AI only through accountability or process rules. |
| [Encouraged](#encouraged) | 5 | The project actively welcomes AI-assisted work. |
| [No published policy](#no-published-policy) | 45 | No AI rule found in CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.md or the PR template. Normal review rules apply. |
| **Total** | **101** | |

3 projects explicitly forbid AI `Co-authored-by` trailers. 8 repos have switched GitHub's pull request creation setting to collaborators only, so outside contributors can only file issues.

## How to disclose

Use the project's own format. These are the common ones.

| Style | Example | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Sentence in the PR description | `This PR was written in part with the assistance of generative AI.` | Kubernetes (trailers forbidden) |
| `Assisted-by:` commit trailer | `Assisted-by: Claude Code (Claude Sonnet 5)` | Linux kernel, LLVM, Mesa, Fedora, GCC, Kubeflow |
| `Generated-by:` commit trailer | `Generated-by: GitHub Copilot` | Mesa, Apache Airflow |
| Free-text extent statement | `This PR was written primarily by Claude Code.` | Model Context Protocol |
| PR template section | Fill in the "Agent context" section with agent and model | PostHog, posthog-js |
| PR label | `llm-generated` | crewAI |

Rules that hold almost everywhere:

- Never put an AI tool in `Signed-off-by`. The Linux kernel forbids it outright, and a DCO sign-off is a human legal statement.
- Do not add `Co-authored-by` for an AI unless the project asks for it (pytest does). Kubernetes, Mesa and promptfoo forbid it.
- Write commit messages, PR descriptions and review replies yourself. Several projects close PRs whose discussion is pasted model output.
- Keep the disclosure short and factual: which tool, what it did, and that you reviewed and tested every change.

Coding agents add attribution by default. Claude Code, for example, appends a `Co-Authored-By` trailer; set `"attribution"` in `.claude/settings.json` to match the target project's format before committing.

## Use the data

```sh
git clone https://github.com/ahmad-punch/awesome-ai-contribution-policies
cd awesome-ai-contribution-policies
npm install          # installs ajv, the only dev dependency
npm run validate     # schema, duplicates, sort order
npm run build        # regenerate this README
```

`policies.json` is a plain array. Each entry has `project`, `repo`, `ecosystem`, `stance`, `agents_allowed`, `disclosure_format`, `co_author_trailer_for_ai`, `gates`, `quote`, `quote_kind`, `source_url` and `last_verified`, plus optional `pr_creation_policy`, `sanctions`, `policy_date` and `notes`. The full contract is [schema/policy.schema.json](schema/policy.schema.json).

## How it works

- `policies.json` is the single source of truth, sorted by project name.
- `scripts/validate.mjs` checks it against the JSON Schema (2020-12) and rejects duplicate repos and unsorted entries.
- `scripts/build-readme.mjs` renders this README. CI fails if the committed README is stale.
- `scripts/check-links.mjs` runs weekly in CI and reports dead source links.

Design notes are in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md).

## Contributing an entry

1. Open a [new policy issue](../../issues/new?template=new-policy.yml) or a [policy change issue](../../issues/new?template=policy-change.yml), or edit `policies.json` directly.
2. Copy the template from [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), link the primary source, and keep the quote under 300 characters.
3. Run `npm run validate && npm run build` and commit both `policies.json` and `README.md`.

- [melissawm/open-source-ai-contribution-policies](https://github.com/melissawm/open-source-ai-contribution-policies): a curated list of AI policies in open source projects.
- [arXiv 2609.07542](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.07542): a study of 281 AI policies across the 2,000 most popular GitHub repositories. 14.9% forbid AI code, 48.8% require disclosure.
